newsitem.title: USA: Hot, dry weather cuts Kansas corn/soy ratings.
newsitem.headline: Hot, dry weather cuts Kansas corn/soy ratings.

text.p: Corn and soybean conditions ratings slipped in the week ended Sunday as hot, dry weather caused heat and moisture stress, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

Corn was rated 74 percent good to excellent, down from 85 percent last week. The crop was silking on 90 percent of the acreage, above the five-year average of 76 percent. Thirty percent of the crop had reached the dough stage, ahead of 21 percent average.
Sorghum was rated 68 percent good to excellent, down from 80 percent the previous week.
The crop was 22 percent headed, above the five-year average of 15 percent.
Soybeans were rated 76 percent good to excellent, against 84 percent last week. The crop was blooming on 75 percent of the acreage, well ahead of average of 48 percent.

Topsoil moisture was rated 17 percent very short, 42 percent short, 36 percent adequate and five percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was rated nine percent very short, 29 percent short, 59 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
